standard_prerequisites.name: Derivation from a set of hypotheses
standard_prerequisites.statement: A derivation of A from Gamma is a finite sequence of formulas ending in A in which every formula is an axiom, an element of Gamma, or follows from earlier lines by a rule of inference.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both hypotheses are unpacked in this form at source lines 848-856, and the concatenated sequence is then verified to be a derivation in the same sense at lines 856-862.

standard_prerequisites.name: Rules of inference and the mixing rule
standard_prerequisites.statement: The axioms and rules of the author's axiomatic system for first-order logic, in particular the rule that licenses a formula whenever a prior line is a conditional whose antecedent is also a prior line.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof's key step replaces each use of the hypothesis A in the second derivation by the corresponding step of the first derivation, appealing to the fact that the same rule of inference still justifies the line (source lines 860-862).

core_obligations: Unpack the second hypothesis: from {A} together with Delta proves B, extract a derivation B_1, ..., B_l = B from {A} union Delta and isolate the steps that are justified by a rule referring to the prior line A (source lines 849-852).
Unpack the first hypothesis: from Gamma proves A, extract a derivation A_1, ..., A_k = A from Gamma where every A_i is an axiom, an element of Gamma, or correct by a rule (source lines 852-856).

Form the concatenation A_1, ..., A_k = A, B_1, ..., B_l = B and verify it is a derivation of B from Gamma union Delta, showing that every line which previously cited A is now justified by the same rule applied to the copy A_k = A of the first part (source lines 856-862).

proof_roadmap.step: Unpack the derivation of B from {A} union Delta and identify the steps that invoke the hypothesis A.
Unpack the derivation of A from Gamma in the standard form (axiom, hypothesis, or rule).
Concatenate the two derivations and check that the result is a derivation of B from Gamma union Delta, re-justifying every former use of A.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own proposition prop:transitivity at source lines 842-846 (with the optional title Transitivity): if Gamma proves A and {A} together with Delta proves B, then Gamma together with Delta proves B. The proof at source lines 848-863 is not a one-line invocation of a stated rule. It has to unpack what a derivation from a set of hypotheses is, note that the intermediate steps of the second derivation which depend on the hypothesis A are justified by rules referring to a prior line equal to A, and then manufacture a single derivation of B from Gamma union Delta by concatenating the two derivations and re-justifying exactly those steps by the same rules now applied to the copy of A that comes from the first derivation. The concatenation is a genuine construction: the two derivations have unrelated lengths and the replacement must be made at every line that cited A. No result outside the retained text is used beyond the definition of a derivation.

compared.difference: prop:reflexivity (statement 822-825, proof 827-829) counts the degenerate case in which a formula is derivable from a set that already contains it; its proof is a one-step appeal to the definition. Our candidate counts the transitivity step, which requires constructing a new derivation out of two given ones and re-justifying the hypothesis-dependent lines.

prop:monotonicity (statement 831-835, proof 837-840) counts the fact that adding hypotheses preserves derivability, which follows by leaving a derivation unchanged. Our candidate changes the derivation by substituting the second hypothesis and is not implied by monotonicity.
